speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To better understand your infant's recurrent stridor and wheezing, can you tell me if these symptoms are worse when the baby cries, feeds, or lies on their back? Also, have there been any episodes of coughing or choking during these events?

speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Laryngotracheomalacia (congenital subglottic stenosis with tracheomalacia). The combination of stridor and wheezing worsening with crying, feeding, and neck flexion, along with post-prandial vomiting, is highly characteristic of this condition due to airway collapse during increased intrathoracic pressure or neck movement. I will request a flexible laryngoscopy and upper airway imaging to confirm the degree of collapse and rule out other causes.
